batch_strategy: Use matched condition panels to investigate newly exposed completion failures, test the structural scope of surprising 2/1 predictions, and constrain endpoint-specific loading responses. Supplement pending CW measurements where an additional condition or loading boundary makes their interpretation substantially more informative.

choices.reason: Measure m118 at 2/1 and 100 uL; predicted V1/V2 is 7.06/13.30 mL. Observed high-loading 4e7e45a513ce579c5ce3 measured 7.95/12.63, whereas 966254b5be3c8ec5edd3 completed at 41.55 at 1/1 and 150 uL. This supplies a missing amount contrast at 2/1 and, with the selected neat-EA midpoint, constrains interpretation of the exceptional 1/1 completion.

Measure m118 in neat EA at 100 uL; predicted 4.84/9.20 mL. Together with the selected 2/1 midpoint and measured 5/1 midpoint 98586ac2d6d266ddb78c, this gives fixed-loading solvent references. It tests whether completion contracts again at the strongest solvent after the large historical V2 underestimate in 966254b5be3c8ec5edd3. The amount difference from that 150-uL anomaly remains explicit.

Measure m133 at 2/1 and 100 uL; predicted 20.32/21.04 mL. Newly measured a7a814c9db59a62411a2 gave 21.63/21.67 at 50 uL, while matched 1/1 midpoint 4ffa7c3e19fe33d7522f gave 5.57/10.42. This tests whether the late shift and nearly coincident endpoints extend beyond one low-loading record, limiting how the model generalizes its newly learned 2/1 response.

Measure m132 at 2/1 and 150 uL; predicted 10.77/11.38 mL. Pending 382ed88009a39dd77794 supplies its exactly matched 10/1 condition. The predicted later onset with stronger solvent and narrow elution interval resemble the newly revealed m133 behavior, but remain unmeasured for m132. This pair tests structural transfer without treating the usual early elution of a nonpolar aromatic as an absolute rule.

Measure m136 at 2/1 and 100 uL; predicted 15.57/17.15 mL. Its measured 20/1 midpoint b6360e1ecf9f6780ce92 was 4.86/7.70, and 5/1 low-loading 7a19ff191dfe91e75bb4 was 6.17/8.63. The large predicted 2/1 onset rise is therefore an informative untested condition response. Comparing this result with m133 and m132 will constrain the scope of corrections across acceptor-free aromatics.

Measure m123 at 1/1 and 100 uL; predicted 4.27/22.20 mL. Pending 6a75887d279501f8d1a9 supplies 150 uL at this ratio. The selected 2/1 and neat-EA midpoints bracket a pronounced model-predicted completion elevation. This label tests both that elevation and the model's nearly flat amount response, informed by the unexpected m118 result rather than by quantile span alone.

Measure m123 at 2/1 and 100 uL; predicted 6.51/8.56 mL. Observed 5/1 midpoint 89d7d7adb1fc72276b1c measured 6.72/10.18. With the selected 1/1 midpoint, this directly tests the predicted jump in completion despite earlier onset. It distinguishes a genuine local solvent response from an unsupported correction propagated through aromatic ether features.

Measure m123 in neat EA at 100 uL; predicted 4.83/6.79 mL. This completes the selected fixed-loading 2/1–1/1–neat-EA panel, anchored by measured 5/1 row 89d7d7adb1fc72276b1c. A terminal label is needed to distinguish a localized 1/1 completion elevation from a broader strong-solvent offset and to supervise ordinary short completion alongside exceptional tails.

Measure m115 at 1/1 and 100 uL; predicted 5.82/22.44 mL. Its matched 2/1 observation f2931e18ce0362f7a6c0 measured 10.02/19.89, and neat-EA low-loading 056a228c0de193b126cf completed at 8.65. Pending 4276fb99ccd1d4c70a06 supplies the 1/1 low boundary. The midpoint tests a predicted completion increase and whether its amount dependence is as small as the model implies.

Measure m194 at 1/1 and 150 uL; predicted 5.14/19.48 mL. Pending c0094343ab6bb16bc58b supplies 50 uL at the same ratio, while the selected neat-EA high boundary holds loading fixed for a solvent contrast. Measured 5/1 midpoint 39815ababe97d7acc107 completed at 26.57. These labels test the predicted amount flatness and completion response of a fused aromatic ether aldehyde.

Measure m194 in neat EA at 150 uL; predicted 4.68/8.18 mL. Paired with its selected 1/1 high boundary, this tests a substantial predicted terminal completion contraction under identical loading conditions. The weaker-solvent observation 39815ababe97d7acc107 provides context at a different amount. This helps establish whether the unusual aldehyde completion behavior has a limited structural and solvent range.

Measure m205 at 2/1 and 150 uL; predicted 27.60/51.02 mL. Matched midpoint c973d4c257be9ef08216 measured 27.63/51.49. The latest 1/1 low boundary b1fcf9bf2e03028d2ef8 was substantially earlier than midpoint 2b10c90b32f970e4b4c8, whereas neat-EA midpoint and high boundary 988724a9391bf1618fda and 0483db40cbad8db07032 were close. This tests whether the model's nearly flat 2/1 amount response is appropriate despite the different 1/1 association.

Measure m204 at 1/1 and 150 uL; predicted 9.53/15.92 mL. Measured low and midpoint rows a3560ac8164465dbb406 and c46b86dae7e6845f08cd changed onset from 10.71 to 9.33 while completion stayed near 16.17. Completing this amount series tests onset saturation and the attenuation relative to the larger measured 2/1 response in 8cc5dd51f0360e578ac3, 53c1be5b96937954b9fa and 6a39aff909ea35989c74.

Measure m19 at 1/1 and 100 uL; predicted 12.78/23.98 mL. Observed boundaries a595d5f1882c39914392 and 97297c71a28a2ccbdeeb measured 15.61/25.51 and 10.81/25.85. The missing midpoint distinguishes onset curvature from an approximately constant completion response. This teaches how a tertiary-amine acrylate differs from the alcohol series under stronger solvent.

Measure m35 at 1/1 and 150 uL; predicted 6.67/17.19 mL. Pending ede92d66c7b35b3b7b8b supplies its matched 2/1 high boundary, and observed 5/1 high boundary 96d0f62092b2b6aec96b measured 4.88/15.75. This tests the predicted local increase in both endpoints with stronger solvent in an aromatic ketone, constraining transfer of solvent-curve corrections beyond methoxy aldehydes.

Measure ethyl acetoacetate m82 at 2/1 and 50 uL; predicted 7.57/15.42 mL. Its measured midpoint 7a3586b45c03832259f5 was 6.43/16.45. Methyl homolog m95 showed a much later low-amount onset followed by a midpoint minimum in 8d018e521e8e6bbc53c2, 8b6fc534edc07d5b79be and b7a9a6b5086135269cb6. This label tests the scope of that response in a frequently represented ester family while retaining differences in density and loading-solvent volume.

hypotheses.content: Recorded amount responses depend on molecule, solvent ratio and endpoint. The newly measured m205 1/1 low-to-midpoint rise contrasts with decreasing onset in m19 and m204, while m205's neat-EA midpoint and high boundary remain close. These are conditional associations and do not isolate an adsorption or loading mechanism.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched labels can teach when density-times-volume should alter onset, completion, both or neither. They also constrain the structural and solvent scope of corrections learned from a large response in one series.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m205 remain nearly flat from 100 to 150 uL at 2/1 despite its 1/1 low-to-midpoint rise, and do the m19 and m204 1/1 onset responses plateau or remain curved?

hypotheses.content: m95's measured 2/1 onset response largely occurs between 50 and 100 uL, while completion has an intermediate minimum. Its fixed-midpoint solvent curve and its differences from m82 require condition-specific supervision; the same amount-response shape cannot yet be transferred to the ethyl homolog under its different recorded loading protocol.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The methyl/ethyl comparison can constrain transfer within a common beta-keto-ester motif without attributing all differences to ester identity. m82 also has many candidate rows, making its missing local amount boundary relevant to Row-distribution accuracy.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is m82's 2/1 low-amount onset appreciably later than its measured midpoint, or is its response substantially smaller than m95's?

hypotheses.content: A localized completion elevation around 1/1 may recur in some oxygenated aromatics, but its occurrence and amplitude are structure- and protocol-specific. m118 at 150 uL and m117 provide measured examples of elevated intermediate-solvent completion. m186 and m198 limit a broad family-level extrapolation. Recurrence in the selected m123, m115, m194 and m35 conditions is untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest m118 failure was concentrated in V2. Bracketed solvent labels and matched pending comparisons can distinguish local completion curvature from a shared aromatic-oxygen offset, preventing both missed tails and excessive transfer of a single exceptional record.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m118 show short completion in neat EA at midpoint loading, and do the predicted 1/1 completion elevations in m123, m115, m194 and m35 survive matched solvent and amount comparisons?

hypotheses.content: The late, nearly coincident endpoints in the new m133 2/1 low-loading record may represent a narrow condition response, but its extension across amounts or to other acceptor-free aromatics is unresolved. The current predictor assigns related 2/1 onset rises to m132 and m136. Their usual weak silica interactions are a chemical prior, not grounds to reject the observed m133 record.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Neighboring labels can determine whether the model's new sharp condition dependence has a useful structural scope or is overgeneralizing an isolated record. This matters for many early-eluting aromatic rows even though the selected predictions are not uniformly high in CW distance.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m133 remain late at 100 uL, does m132 become later at 2/1 than its pending matched 10/1 condition, and does m136 exhibit its predicted large 2/1 onset rise?

feedback_interpretation:
The latest m118 results overturn the previous strong-solvent contraction extrapolation at high loading. Its measured 150-uL sequence is 10.13/26.12 mL at 5/1, 7.95/12.63 at 2/1, and 5.32/41.55 at 1/1. The last record had a historical V2 error of -30.52 mL while onset was close to prediction. This establishes a serious acquisition-time completion failure, but one record does not establish reproducibility or mechanism. I therefore select available neighboring conditions and test the scope of analogous current-model solvent-curve predictions. For the m118 5/1 midpoint I use observed 98586ac2d6d266ddb78c; the previously cited 985361f6699d97f9464f is m60 and cannot support an aldehyde comparison.

The actual m205 low boundary measured 10.51/25.36, compared with 18.27/33.28 at the midpoint and 16.77/34.09 at high loading. Thus a uniformly decreasing amount response is inappropriate for this measured 1/1 series. Its neat-EA high result, 5.82/10.85, closely matches the measured midpoint and supports a much smaller response there. m204's new 2/1 midpoint shows most onset decline occurring before 100 uL, with completion slightly below the high boundary; its 1/1 low-to-midpoint completion is nearly unchanged. m95 likewise shows onset saturation and an intermediate completion minimum, motivating a homolog boundary rather than another dense m95 interpolation.

m117's low boundary extends its measured 1/1 completion increase across amounts. m186's new 5/1 high boundary supports a gradual contraction into its stronger-solvent sequence, and m198 retains small completion amount contrasts. These outcomes limit any shared aldehyde correction. CW's m133 2/1 low boundary, 21.63/21.67, is a new failure region in an otherwise early-eluting hydrocarbon series and motivates neighboring-amount and structural-transfer tests. All error statements refer to acquisition-time predictions, not current residuals.
batch_rationale:
These sixteen distinct candidate IDs supplement the unchanged sixteen pending CW IDs without overlap. Selection and all supplied premeasurement predictions are fixed before any new label reveal.

The largest part of the batch investigates endpoint-specific solvent curvature. The m118 pair follows a severe new V2 failure using the available midpoint conditions. The three m123 labels form a fixed-loading solvent panel around its predicted 1/1 elevation. m115 and m194 add useful amount comparisons to pending 1/1 measurements, and m194's matched neat-EA boundary tests the terminal contraction. The m35 condition uses a pending matched 2/1 row to test how far such corrections should extend across aromatic carbonyl structures. These panels can teach both ordinary contraction and local exceptions without imposing either as a universal rule.

The three acceptor-free aromatic selections test whether the surprising m133 response extends across amounts and structures. The m132 choice also creates an exact loading match with a pending solvent condition. The alcohol and amine selections resolve conditional onset slopes, while the m82 low boundary tests transfer from the recently clarified m95 amount curve into a heavily represented ester family.

The batch uses chemical similarity and pending measurements to make specific comparisons informative, rather than treating similarity as automatic redundancy. Expected benefit comes from supervising conditional slopes, limiting the scope of corrections, and distinguishing V1 changes from V2 changes across recurring Row motifs. Quantile spans are outputs of one predictor and are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. V2 minus V1 is the elution interval width. Within-tuple disagreement elsewhere in the observations and missing experimental variables limit mechanistic conclusions.
